card.name: Explaining why a risk cannot be eliminated
card.fires_on: Linking words and commas right after a statement that a safeguard is imperfect, such as "Despite these measures," or "there is still some risk because". It marks the point where a remaining, unavoidable limitation is about to be stated.

modes.label: Because / despite clause
modes.description: The word or comma that introduces the reason a risk remains despite screening or safety steps.
modes.example: Despite these measures<<,>> this product can still potentially transmit disease.

modes.label: Inside the limitation clause
modes.description: Words within a clause saying a method is not perfect or not absolute.
modes.example: These measures do<< not>> eliminate the risk of transmitting these or other

modes.label: Failure statements
modes.description: The verb or subject in a statement that a method can fail or a test cannot detect something.

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words meaning inevitably, unavoidable or imperfect, as in "the risk is inevitably still present".
card.plain: It fires where the text is explaining that a safeguard is not perfect, so some risk unavoidably remains.
